Why Ingredient Choice Matters
Converting grams (mass) to cups (volume) depends entirely on density. For example, 100g of All-Purpose Flour equals 0.833 cups, whereas 100g of Honey equals only 0.298 cups.

Common Grams to Cups Conversions

Converting grams to cups depends on ingredient density. Below is a quick conversion reference table for 100 grams across common baking ingredients using US Customary Cups (236.6 mL).

Ingredient State / Method 100 Grams Equals Practical Measure Reference Density
All-Purpose Flour Spooned & leveled 0.833 cups ≈ ¾ cup + 1 tbsp + 1 tsp 120g / cup (King Arthur)
Granulated Sugar Granulated, dry 0.505 cups ≈ ½ cup 198g / cup (King Arthur)
Butter Solid / softened 0.441 cups ≈ 7 tbsp (0.88 sticks) 227g / cup (King Arthur)
Brown Sugar Firmly packed 0.469 cups ≈ ½ cup - 1 tbsp 213g / cup (King Arthur)
Powdered Sugar Unsifted 0.885 cups ≈ ⅞ cup 113g / cup (King Arthur)
Rolled Oats Dry rolled oats 1.124 cups ≈ 1 ⅛ cups 89g / cup (King Arthur)
Uncooked Rice Dry long grain 0.541 cups ≈ ½ cup + 1 tbsp 185g / cup (USDA)
Honey Liquid 0.298 cups ≈ ¼ cup + 1 tbsp 336g / cup (King Arthur)
Vegetable / Olive Oil Liquid 0.463 cups ≈ ½ cup - 1 tbsp 216g / cup (USDA)
Whole Milk Liquid 0.410 cups ≈ 6.5 tbsp 244g / cup (USDA)

Why Sourcing & Measuring Method Matter

A common cause of failed baking recipes is the assumption that 1 cup of flour has a fixed, universal weight. In reality, King Arthur Baking lists all-purpose flour at 120 grams per cup using the spoon-and-level technique, while the USDA Food Buying Guide lists enriched white flour at 125 grams per cup.

If you scoop flour directly from a bag with a measuring cup, you compress the flour grains, packing up to 140 grams into a single cup. That 20g difference is enough to make cakes dry and tough. Our converter explicitly reveals the exact measurement state and primary reference source for every output.
